neighbours.label: Specialized vocabulary for striated muscle proteins and contractile structures, including troponin in cardiac biomarker contexts.
fire: During the emergency assessment, elevated troponin suggested damage to the patient's heart muscle.
After reviewing the blood results, the cardiologist noted that troponins remained elevated overnight.
In the physiology lecture, tropomyosin was described as a protein that helps regulate muscle contraction.
Beneath the microscope, the student identified striated muscle by its alternating light and dark bands.
During heating, sarcoplasmic proteins in the meat sample began to lose their normal folded shapes.
On the electron micrograph, Z lines marked the boundaries of the repeating contractile units.
Within each muscle fiber, myofibrils formed long bundles aligned with the direction of contraction.
For the laboratory diagram, actin filaments were drawn as thin strands inside the muscle fiber.
quiet: At the hospital, elevated blood markers suggested damage to the patient's heart muscle.
By morning rounds, the physician reported that markers of heart injury remained elevated overnight.
According to the lecture notes, several regulatory proteins help control when muscle contraction begins.
Through the microscope, the trainee recognized muscle tissue by its alternating light and dark bands.
As the meat sample warmed, proteins in its cellular fluid began losing their normal folded shapes.
In the enlarged image, dark boundary markings separated the repeating contractile units of the muscle.
Inside the muscle cell, long bundles of fine threads followed the direction in which it shortened.
To complete the laboratory illustration, the student added thin protein strands within the muscle cell.
